div.head: VI As 8.4
div.ab: ⁊ gif man spór gespirige of scyre on oðre, fon þa menn tó þe þar nycst syndon ⁊ drifan þæt spór, oð hit man þam gerefan gecyðe: fó hé syððan tó mid his monunge ⁊ adrife þæt spór út of his scíre, gif he mage; gif he þonne ne mæge, forgylde þæt yrfe angylde. ⁊ habban þa gerefscypas begen þa fullan spæce gemæne, si swa hwær swa hit sy, swa be norðan mearce swa be suðan: á of scire on oðre þæt ælc gerefa fylste oðrum to ure ealra friðe, be cynges oferhyrnesse.

Et si uestigium minetur ab una scyra in aliam, excipiant hoc qui propiores (proximiores) aderunt et educant illud uestigium; uel indicetur preposito: et ipse postea suscipiat cum monicione sua et minet uestigium illud extra scyram suam, si possit; si non possit, reddat ipsum pecus uno gildo. Et habeant ambe prepositure placitum hoc (questionis huius) in communi, sit alterutrum quod sit, sic a septentrionali merca sic ab australi: semper de scyra in aliam (scyram) omnis prepositus adiuuet alium ad pacem omnium nostrum per regis ouerhyrnessam.

⁊ gif man spór gespirige of scyre on oðre, fon þa menn tó þe þar nycst syndon ⁊ drifan þæt spór, oð hit man þam gerefan gecyðe: fó hé syððan tó mid his monunge ⁊ adrife þæt spór út of his scíre, gif he mage; gif he þonne ne mæge, forgylde þæt yrfe angylde. ⁊ habban þa gerefscypas begen þa fullan spæce gemæne, si swa hwær swa hit sy, swa be norðan mearce swa be suðan, á of scire on oðre—þæt ælc gerefa fylste oðrum to ure ealra friðe, be cynges oferhyrnesse.

Und wenn man die Spur [verlorenen Viehs] von einer Grafschaft in die andere verfolgt, so sollen die Leute, welche dort zunächst wohnen, [sie] aufnehmen und die Spur verfolgen, bis man es dem [Grafschafts]vogt künde: der nehme sie dann mit seinem Bezirk[svolke] auf und leite die Spur aus seiner Grafschaft hinaus, wenn er kann; wenn er [das] aber nicht kann, bezahle er das Vieh mit einfachem Ersatz. Und es erhalten beide Sheriffsämter [das, wo Eigenthümer wohnt, und das des Spurendes] die ganze Klagesache gemeinsam, sei es, wo immer es sei, entweder nördlich der Grenze [unserer Grafschaft] oder südlich: dass immer aus einer Grafschaft in die andere jeder [Grafschafts-]vogt dem anderen helfe zu unser aller Polizeiordnung bei [Strafe der Busse für] Ungehorsam gegen den König.

And if the track [of lost cattle] is followed from one shire into another, then the men who live nearest there are to take [it] up and follow the track until it is reported to the [shire-]reeve: let him then take it up with the [people of his] district and lead the track out of his shire, if he can; but if he cannot [do that], let him pay for the cattle with single compensation. And both sheriffdoms [that where the owner lives and that where the track ends] are to have the whole suit in common, wherever it may be, whether north of the boundary [of our shire] or south: so that always from one shire to another every [shire-]reeve help the other for the peace of us all, on [pain of the fine for] disobedience to the king.

And if anyone traces a trail from one district to another, the men who are nearest shall take up the trail, follow it until it can be brought to the notice of the reeve. Afterwards, he, with the men under his jurisdiction, shall take up the trail and follow it, if he can, to the boundary of his district. If, however, he cannot, he shall pay the value of the cattle, and the whole case shall be undertaken by the authorities of the two districts in common, wheresoever it may happen that a trail passes from one district to another, whether to the north or the south of our borders—all reeves shall help one another to maintain the security upon which we are all dependent or pay the fine for insubordination to the king.

And if one follows a trail from one shire into another, the men who are nearest are to take up and follow the trail, until it is announced to the reeve; he then is to take it up with [the men of] his district, and follow the trail out of his shire, if he can; if, however, he cannot, he is to pay the price of the cattle, and the two reeves’ districts are to have the full suit in common, no matter where it is, whether north of the boundary or south; so that even from one shire to another each reeve is to help the next for the sake of the peace of us all, on pain of the [fine for] disobedience to the king.

Q setzt uel, wohl oð verwechselnd mit oððe, irrig: der Sheriff tritt nicht neben den Grenzbauern auf, sondern führt sie; ebenso Hu 5
Q puts uel, probably confusing oð with oððe, wrongly: the sheriff does not appear alongside the border peasants but leads them; likewise Hu 5
‘Bann, Aufgebot’ Schmid. Diese Bed. scheint nicht belegt. — Die Übs. hätte genauer den Sinn getroffen mit ‘der beginne die Spur zu leiten’
‘ban, levy’ Schmid. This meaning does not seem to be attested. — The translation would have caught the sense more exactly with ‘let him begin to lead the trail’

Spurfolge 4a. c. Von der Haftung des Grundherrn spricht V 2 noch nicht, wohl aber Duns und III Em 6. So braucht nicht, wie Schmid 636 annimmt, ein Privileg Londons vorzuliegen; sondern vermutlich aus einem uns verlorenen Gesetz mit geändertem Landrecht fliesst die öffentlich-rechtliche Drohung gegen fremde Sheriffs zu Ende von 8, 4

Spurfolge 4a. c. V 2 does not yet speak of the liability of the lord of the manor, but Duns and III Em 6 do. So there is no need to assume, as Schmid 636 does, a privilege of London; rather, the public-law threat against the sheriffs of other shires at the end of 8, 4 probably derives from a law, lost to us, that altered the general law of the land
den Justizertrag über das Ersatzgeld hinaus. Der Sprengel steht für den ihn dem Staate abpachtenden Verwalter auch Af 37, 1². III Atr 3, 2f.
the judicial revenue over and above the compensation money. The district stands for the administrator who farms it from the State also in Af 37, 1². III Atr 3, 2f.

Möglich, dass diese Worte dem Reichsgesetze (o.⁴; u. 8, 9⁸) entstammen, also ‘zur inneren Sicherheit der Nation’ bedeuten. Meist aber wird hier deutlich nur des Landfriedensbundes Partikularfriede gemeint, wie u. 8, 7. 8, 9

It is possible that these words derive from the national law (above⁴; below 8, 9⁸) and thus mean ‘for the internal security of the nation’. Generally, however, only the particular peace of the peace-league is clearly meant here, as below 8, 7. 8, 9
120 Schill.; so III Em 6, 2. Für denselben Ungehorsam (s. d. Gl 6) würde der Hundredvorsteher nur 30 Schill. Strafe zahlen; Hu 5, 1
120 shill.; so III Em 6, 2. For the same disobedience (see that word in Gl 6) the hundred-man would pay a fine of only 30 shill.; Hu 5, 1

scyre is clearly the sphere of jurisdiction of a gerefa (cf. cap. 10, below). It is not clear whether the gerefa mentioned here and in the two preceding paragraphs is what was later called scirgerefa, i.e. sheriff. If that were the case it might be inferred that the scir was a county. It may, however, denote a smaller division of territory, possibly the divisions belonging to the reeves mentioned in the preamble.
